reviews.comment: Be ready to study by Wikipedia
The teaching makes no sense, be ready to study absolutely by yourself.
Nice guy but he truly can not teach in lecture. Everything I have done the entire semester was reading the book and learning by myself.

Struggled to understand him 80% of the time due to his accent and how soft-spoken he is. He was helpful during his office hours. Did a lot of self-learning through ppts, the textbook, and Pearson homework. The homework was quite much but searching online helped. He was also very flexible and offered extensions whenever we needed or asked.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is not terrible, but you do have to study outside of class because his lectures are a little boring. I found Spartan Tutoring on YouTube to very helpful when studying for exams. University Physics grading is strange at first, but Professor Ko is very nice and wants everyone to do well in his class. He won't test over something you don't know.

Dude just sucks, can barely understand him, he talks slow, seems like a nice guy but oh my god hes a bad instructor, make simple concepts more confusing, I wish he didnt have iclicker so I could skip and just use the textbook

Professor Ko is really kind and welcoming. However, his lectures are very monotone and consist of reading a screen of scattered numbers. He is very receptive to questions in and out of class, however sometimes you can't ask a question about every single slide. Only recommend if you already are good at physics/AP Physics.

Honestly, he is a very nice prof and seems to care about his students, but his lectures are awful. He takes forever to explain simple things, the examples are scatterbrained and its hard to understand what hes saying a lot of the time and he tends to go over time. The only thing that somehow saved me in this class was the learning objectives.
Dont choose this course, its absolutely a waste of time.

This course is just a parody of courses given by math department. This professor looks meticulous when teaching but impact nothing not only due to his extremely ambiguous pronunciation, but also his awful slides, which always contain prolix and difficult-to-read statements and formula. In a word, this course is a waste of time.
This professor is willing to help students. However, his talk is difficult to understand and his notes and homework are not good stuff for studying.

Two things about Ko, he is extremely nice and extremely smart. He is not the best teacher however, he is incredibly hard to understand in class, I sat in the front row sometimes and still couldn't hear him. However, I also went to his office hours at least 15 times, and in these he is extremely helpful for understanding difficult concepts.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's good. Hard to understand with his accent though admittedly. If you are good at physics and can understand it conceptually, you'll be alright. Ko does try very hard to teach, although he can be all over the place and hard to follow. The pre-lectures before class do a good job at teaching the material though. You learn more from there.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Ko definitely tried his best to be accessible and help his students. In lecture, he wasn't terrible, but he wasn't great either. He is fairly quiet and monotone, so it was difficult to want to pay attention if you went. But PHYS218 lectures are 100% useless. I learned everything from my recitation leader and from the prelectures
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Ko was a very caring professor. He really tried to be helpful, and wanted lectures to be helpful, but they just were not. I went to class and that seemed to get me on his good side, but he had trouble working technology and leading lectures. The upside of that was we all got full credit for the clicker questions.

The bad: Difficult to understand at first with his accent. Sit towards the front. You'll learn to understand him with a bit of time  The good: One of the most caring & generous professors ever. He's very giving of his time if you show that you're making an effort. The subject matter is extremely difficult, but he's willing to help if you'll ask
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice guy. His class is almost the same as the textbook. Just read the textbook and be familiar with formulas. Mastering homework needs some time. But his tests are easy. Have four common exams and a final. Got 88 for first exam, 100 for other two and 98 for the last exam. Final only has 9 questions and 2 from each common exam.

Professor Ko seems to be a very intelligent man. That being said, he's an awful professor. His lectures are very confusing through his thick accent, and he speaks so quietly you can barely hear him, even sitting in the front. On the first test the class average was a 45. All other PHYS201 professors had an average of around 65. DO NOT TAKE
